title: One-year follow-up of accelerated transepithelial corneal collagen cross-linking for progressive pediatric keratoconus

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License)

groups.description: 18 eyes of 17 patients aged 10-17 years with progressive keratoconus treated with accelerated transepithelial (epithelium-on) cross-linking, 45 mW/cm2 pulsed UV-A for 5 min 20 s (Methods)

series.notes: mean ± SD; Pentacam (Methods); the table gives no unit, dioptres from the Abstract and the inclusion criterion (>= 1.00 D increase in maximal keratometry)

exclusions.what: Results text: numbers of eyes with Kmax decreased, stable or increased at 12 months

exclusions.reason: single case shown as an example; figure only

notes: Every patient completed the 1-year follow-up (Methods); the article reports no larger treated group.
Consent from a parent or legal guardian; inclusion age 10-17 years.
Table 2 footnote describes K1 as steepest and K2 as flattest meridian keratometry; neither is used.
Refraction and BCVA (Table 1), K1, K2 and thinnest corneal thickness (Table 2) and posterior elevation (Figures 1, 2) are reported and not used.
